A wire of resistance \(R\) and length \(L\) is cut into 5 equal parts. If these parts are joined parallely, then resultant resistance will be : 

 

[JEE Main 2024, 27 Jan (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
When resistors are connected in parallel, the reciprocal of the equivalent resistance is the sum of the reciprocals of the individual resistances. For 5 equal resistors in parallel, the formula is:


\(\frac{1}{R_{e q}}=\frac{1}{R_1}+\frac{1}{R_2}+\frac{1}{R_3}+\frac{1}{R_4}+\frac{1}{R_5}\)


Since all 5 parts have the same resistance \(\boldsymbol{R}^{\prime}\), the formula becomes:


\(\frac{1}{R_{e q}}=\frac{1}{R^{\prime}}+\frac{1}{R^{\prime}}+\frac{1}{R^{\prime}}+\frac{1}{R^{\prime}}+\frac{1}{R^{\prime}}=\frac{5}{R^{\prime}}\)

\(R_{e q}=\frac{R^{\prime}}{5}\)

\(\begin{aligned}
&R_{e q}=\frac{R / 5}{5}=\frac{R}{25}
\end{aligned}\)

didt=ddt(i0sin(ωt))=i0ωcos(ωt)\frac{di}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt} (i_0 \sin(\omega t)) = i_0 \omega \cos(\omega t)

Substitute this into the emf equation:

e=Mi0ωcos(ωt)e = M i_0 \omega \cos(\omega t)

The maximum value of the induced emf (emax) occurs when cos(ωt)=1:

emax=Mi0ωe_{\text{max}} = M i_0 \omega

Now, substitute the provided values (M = 0.002 H, i0=5A,ω=50π rad/s):

emax=0.002×5×50πe_{\text{max}} = 0.002 \times 5 \times 50\pi
emax=0.01×50πe_{\text{max}} = 0.01 \times 50\pi
emax=0.5π=π2 Ve_{\text{max}} = 0.5\pi = \frac{\pi}{2}\text{ V}

The problem states the maximum emf is πα V.

Comparing π2 with πα:

α=2

\(f(x)-f(y)\leq\log_e\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)+x-y\).

Combining both inequalities,

\(f(x)-f(y)=\log_e\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)+x-y\).

For fixed \(y\), differentiating with respect to \(x\),

\(\displaystyle f'(x)=\dfrac1x+1\).

Therefore,

\(\displaystyle f'\left(\dfrac1{n^2}\right)=n^2+1\).

Hence,

\(\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{20}f'\left(\dfrac1{n^2}\right)=\sum_{n=1}^{20}n^2+20\).

Using

\(\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{20}n^2=\dfrac{20\cdot21\cdot41}{6}=2870\),

we get

\(2870+20=2890\).

If \(\alpha\) satisfies the equation \(x^2+x+1=0\) and \((1+\alpha)^7= A + B \alpha+ C \alpha^2, A , B , C \geqslant 0\), then \(5(3 A -2 B - C )\) is equal to _________.

 

[JEE Main 2024, 27 Jan (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Given \(x^2+x+1=0\).

So, the roots are \(\omega\) and \(\omega^2\), where \(\omega^3=1\) and \(1+\omega+\omega^2=0\).

Let \(\alpha\) be one root of \(x^2+x+1=0\).

Then,

\(\alpha^2+\alpha+1=0\)

\(\Rightarrow 1+\alpha=-\alpha^2\)

Now,

\((1+\alpha)^7=(-\alpha^2)^7\)

\(\Rightarrow (1+\alpha)^7=-\alpha^{14}\)

Since \(\alpha^3=1\),

\(\alpha^{14}=\alpha^{12}\cdot\alpha^2=(\alpha^3)^4\cdot\alpha^2=\alpha^2\)

So,

\((1+\alpha)^7=-\alpha^2\)

Using \(\alpha^2+\alpha+1=0\),

\(-\alpha^2=1+\alpha\)

Therefore,

\((1+\alpha)^7=1+\alpha\)

Comparing with \(A+B\alpha+C\alpha^2\),

\(A=1,\ B=1,\ C=0\)

Hence,

\(5(3A-2B-C)=5(3-2-0)\)

\(\Rightarrow 5(3A-2B-C)=5\)

questions.question:
If the solution of the differential equation \((2 x+3 y-2) d x+(4 x+6 y-7) d y=0, y(0)=3\), is \(\alpha x+\beta y+3 \log _e|2 x+3 y-\gamma|=6\), then \(\alpha+2 \beta+3 \gamma\) is equal to _________.

 

[JEE Main 2024, 27 Jan (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(u=2x+3y\).

The differential equation becomes

\((u-2)\,dx+(2u-7)\,dy=0\)

The given form of the solution is

\(\alpha x+\beta y+3\ln|u-\gamma|=6\)

Differentiating, we get

\(\left(\alpha+\dfrac{6}{u-\gamma}\right)dx+\left(\beta+\dfrac{9}{u-\gamma}\right)dy=0\)

The ratio of the coefficients must satisfy

\(\dfrac{\alpha(u-\gamma)+6}{\beta(u-\gamma)+9}=\dfrac{u-2}{2u-7}\)

Cross-multiplying, we get

\([\alpha(u-\gamma)+6](2u-7)=[\beta(u-\gamma)+9](u-2)\)

Comparing the coefficients of \(u^2\), \(u\) and the constant terms, we get

\(2\alpha-\beta=0\)

\(\Rightarrow \beta=2\alpha\)

\(-2\alpha\gamma-7\alpha+\beta\gamma+2\beta+3=0\)

\(\Rightarrow -3\alpha+3=0\)

\(\Rightarrow \alpha=1\)

\(\Rightarrow \beta=2\)

\(7\alpha\gamma-2\beta\gamma-24=0\)

\(\Rightarrow 7\gamma-4\gamma-24=0\)

\(\Rightarrow \gamma=8\)

The initial condition \(y(0)=3\) gives the constant \(6\), so the given solution form is consistent.

\(\Rightarrow \alpha+2\beta+3\gamma=1+4+24=29\)

questions.question:
A fair die is tossed repeatedly until a six is obtained. Let \(X\) denote the number of tosses required and let \(a=P(X=3), b=P(X \geqslant 3)\) and \(c=P(X \geqslant 6 \mid X>3)\). Then \(\frac{b+c}{a}\) is equal to _________.

 

[JEE Main 2024, 27 Jan (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(F\) denote failure to obtain \(6\) on a toss.

For a fair die, \(P(F)=\dfrac56\).

\(\displaystyle a=P(X=3)=\left(\dfrac56\right)^2\left(\dfrac16\right)=\dfrac{25}{216}\)

\(\displaystyle b=P(X\geq3)=\left(\dfrac56\right)^2=\dfrac{25}{36}\)

Given \(X>3\), the first three tosses are failures.

For \(X\geq6\), the fourth and fifth tosses must also be failures.

\(\displaystyle c=P(X\geq6\mid X>3)=\left(\dfrac56\right)^2=\dfrac{25}{36}\)

\(\displaystyle \dfrac{b+c}{a}=\dfrac{\frac{25}{36}+\frac{25}{36}}{\frac{25}{216}}\)

\(\displaystyle \Rightarrow \dfrac{b+c}{a}=\dfrac{25}{18}\cdot\dfrac{216}{25}=12\)
